bib.title: ViperGPT: Visual Inference via Python Execution for Reasoning

question: Can a code-generating LLM compose pretrained vision and language modules into per-query Python programs that answer visual queries without any task-specific training?
hypothesis: Explicit programmatic composition with an interpreter gives interpretable, logical, training-free visual reasoning that matches or beats end-to-end zero-shot models.
contributions: A framework integrating code-generation models into vision with an API and the Python interpreter
State-of-the-art zero-shot results on visual grounding, image QA and video QA
A Python library for program synthesis on visual tasks, to be open-sourced

method.summary: Codex (code-davinci-002) receives an API specification (signatures, docstrings, query-code examples) plus the query and emits a Python function execute_command, which is run by the Python interpreter. Functions call pretrained models (GLIP, X-VLM, MiDaS, BLIP-2, GPT-3). No training or fine-tuning.
method.task: zero-shot visual grounding, compositional image QA, outside-knowledge QA, video causal/temporal QA

datasets.name: NExT-QA
datasets.split: multiple-choice version; hard split T/C and full set

inference.prompting: API specification (class/method signatures, docstrings, query-code example pairs) followed by the query; per-benchmark subset of the API and benchmark-specific examples (Listings 1-5); optional context given as a comment before generation (Sec 5.3)

parameters.modules per benchmark: RefCOCO: ImagePatch methods except best_text_match and simple_query, plus distance; GQA: Listing 1 up to llm_query, not used; OK-VQA: only simple_query and llm_query; NeXT-QA: VideoSegment, find, exists, best_text_match, simple_query, best_image_match, select_answer

other.execution: each program in a generated batch run simultaneously with multiprocessing; producer-consumer design for GPU batching
other.video input: video provided as ordered list of images; frame count and sampling not stated

metrics.name: accuracy / IoU
metrics.definition: Table 1 header reads IoU (%) but caption says accuracy on REC; other tables accuracy

eval.protocol: Single run per benchmark as far as stated; no seeds, sample counts or significance tests reported

prompts.text:
# chair at the front
def execute_command(image) -> ImagePatch:
    # Return the chair
    image_patch = ImagePatch(image)
    chair_patches = image_patch.find("chair")
    chair_patches.sort(key=lambda chair: chair.compute_depth())
    chair_patch = chair_patches[0]
    # Remember: return the chair
    return chair_patch

limits: No temperature, sampling, max tokens, number of programs per query or example counts in the prompt are stated, so the run cannot be reproduced exactly from the text
Dataset sizes and exact splits not given (only RefCOCO/RefCOCO+ testA, GQA test-dev named)
Appendix A promised experimental setup details but only lists model versions
Zero-shot still well below supervised on RefCOCO (72.0 vs OFA 94.0) and GQA (48.1 vs CRF 72.1)
Relies on code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003, since deprecated
Prompt examples are benchmark-specific, so 'zero-shot' means no training but tailored API examples
Paper shows cosmetically cleaned programs (comments and error handling removed)
In-the-wild results (Fig 1) are qualitative with no quantitative evaluation
